rows.text: The search for a new ship’s cook is over: the result of Advertisement No. NAU/GAL/017/2026 is out. The galley is cautiously optimistic.
Post-doctoral fellowship in Advanced Map Reading: applications open. Candidates must be able to hold a map the right way up.
Ph.D. shortlist is up for Humanities and Social Sciences. Welcome to the map-drawing years.
The Winter Research Internship is now boarding. Bring a jacket. The ship has no heating.
Annual lifeboat inspection. Every department must confirm where its lifeboat is. Two have already asked what a lifeboat is.
Ph.D. viva for Gold D. Roger, in Gold D. Roger Hall, 11:30 AM. He is also the examiner. Fair winds.
Scholarship notice, with step-by-step instructions for applying on the student portal.
International Conference on Navigation Without Instruments (NWI-2026). Attendance is expected to be scattered.
Mid-semester exams: where to sit. Bring a pen and an umbrella.
Official Language Week 2026. Events in every language spoken on board, including Parrot.
Four new interest groups: Knot Theory, Tide Modelling, Sail Materials and Cartography. Meetings are wherever the ship is.
Gold Medal awardees for 2026. Actual gold, for once.
One anchor. Any anchor, really
40 hammocks for Hostel Block C. Must survive engineering students
